tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.gradium.ai/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Voice Design

> Create a voice from a written description, audition it, and convert it into a voice you can use everywhere

Voice Design creates natural, realistic voices from a text description.
Describe the character you want for your voice agent or product, and Gradium
generates a few candidates. You listen, then convert the one you like into a
permanent voice. From then on it works like any other `voice_id`: REST,
WebSocket and Speech-to-Speech. No reference audio is needed.

<Card title="Have a recording instead?" icon="microphone" href="/guides/voices/custom-voices">
  Custom voices clone a speaker from a short audio sample.
</Card>

## How it works

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="1. Generate" icon="wand-magic-sparkles">

  <Card title="2. Listen" icon="headphones">

  <Card title="3. Convert" icon="bookmark">

Describe the voice in one or two sentences, up to 500 characters, in English,
French, Spanish, Portuguese or German. Gradium expands the description into a

character, change the description.

| Audition a candidate | `POST /post/speech/tts` |
| Convert a candidate | `POST /voices/from-embedding` |
| Delete a candidate | `DELETE /voice-generator/embeddings/{embedding_id}` |

Auditioning a candidate or synthesising with a converted voice is an ordinary
TTS request, so everything in [Voice Settings](/guides/voice-settings) applies.
See [Model selection](/guides/text-to-speech#model-selection) for TTS model access.

```json theme={null}
{
  "text": "Hi there, thanks so much for calling Northgate!",
  "voice_id": "vox_emb_njsiEgpj5NjHKdZc",
  "output_format": "wav",
  "only_audio": true,
  "json_config": { "temp": 0.5 }
}
```

### Temperature (`temp`)

`0.0` to `1.4`, default `0.7`.

* **Audition at the default.** `0.0` makes a lively voice sound flatter than it will in production.
* **`0.3` to `0.5`** for scripted, high-volume output where takes must match: IVR prompts, fixed announcements.
* **Default or slightly above** for conversational agents and narration.

## Supported tags

The models read plain text. Two inline tags are recognised, on candidates and
converted voices alike. **Anything else is spoken aloud as text.**

| Tag | Effect |
| - | - |
| `<break time="1.5s" />` | A pause of `0.1` to `2.0` seconds. Surround the tag with spaces. |
| `<flush>` | Emit audio for all text received so far. Only meaningful when streaming over the WebSocket. |

On a candidate, tags count toward the 100-character limit.

SSML is not interpreted. `<speak><prosody rate="slow">Hello there.</prosody></speak>`
produces a voice saying "speak prosody rate slow, hello there, slash prosody,

| - | - |

| `<prosody pitch>`, `<prosody volume>` | The description. Pitch and energy are attributes of the voice. |

| `<say-as>`, `<sub>`, `<phoneme>` | [`rewrite_rules`](/guides/text-rewriting) or a [pronunciation dictionary](/api-reference/endpoint/create-pronunciation) |
| `<voice>` | A separate request with a different `voice_id` |

Markdown and HTML are read as text too. Strip formatting before sending.

| | |
| - | - |
| **Retention** | Candidates are removed 30 days after generation. Converting one clears its expiry. |
| **Accumulation** | Generating never evicts earlier candidates. Holding them is free. |
| **Cleanup** | `DELETE /voice-generator/embeddings/{embedding_id}`. Always safe: a converted voice holds its own copy. Unknown id: `404`. |
| **Deleting a voice** | `DELETE /voices/{voice_id}` leaves the candidate intact, with no expiry. It can be converted again. |
| **Lost an id** | `GET /voice-generator/embeddings` lists every candidate, newest first, with its description. Page with `skip` and `limit` (1 to 1000, default 100). `expires_at: null` marks converted candidates. |

## Limits

| Limit | Value |
| - | - |
| Description | 1 to 500 characters |
| Candidates per request | 1 to 5, default 1 |
| Audition text | 100 characters, REST only |
| Languages | `en`, `fr`, `es`, `pt`, `de` |
| Candidate retention | 30 days, cleared once converted |
| Converted voices | Count against the custom-voice allowance |

## Errors

Errors are `{"detail": "..."}`, except `422`, which carries a list of field errors.

| Status | Where | Meaning |
| - | - | - |
| `400` | Audition | Text over 100 characters |
| `401` | Any | Invalid or expired API key |
| `404` | Audition, delete | Unknown, not ready, or another account's id |
| `409` | Convert | Already converted, not ready, or custom-voice allowance reached. `detail` says which. |
| `422` | Generate, list | Invalid `language`, `n_samples`, `prompt` or `limit` |

A candidate that never becomes ready is almost always a `json_config` value out
of range or a key the API does not recognise. See [the
allow-list](#the-json_config-allow-list).

lastPrompt: does gradium has ability to design voice on the fly?

content.text:
Yes. Gradium calls it **Voice Design**: you write a description of the voice and it generates a new one, with no reference audio needed. But you create the voice once and then reuse it. You can't restyle the voice on each request.

**How it works** ([guide](https://docs.gradium.ai/guides/voices/voice-design.md)):
1. `POST /voice-generator/generate` with `{"prompt": "...", "language": "de", "n_samples": 3}`. The description can be up to 500 characters, and you get 1–5 candidate voices back.
2. The candidates are generated in the background and are ready in a few seconds. Check with `GET /voice-generator/embeddings?embedding_id=...`.
3. Listen to a candidate with ordinary TTS, using its id as the `voice_id`. Previews are limited to 100 characters and work over REST only.
4. `POST /voices/from-embedding` turns the one you like into a permanent `voice_id`. It then works over REST, WebSocket streaming and speech-to-speech.

**Limits that matter for using it live:**
- **Not instant.** You have to wait until the candidates are ready, and you can't use one in production until you convert it.
- **Not repeatable.** Every request produces a new voice, so sending the same prompt again won't give you the same voice back. Keep the ids you want.
- **Per-request control is small.** You only get `temp` (how varied the delivery is, 0–1.4), `padding_bonus` (speed) and rewrite rules. Pitch and energy are fixed by the description. SSML is not read, so tags like `<prosody>` get spoken aloud. The only tags it understands are `<break time="..."/>` and `<flush>`.
- **Languages:** en, fr, es, pt, de. **Italian is not supported**, which matters if you need all of SBB's languages.
- **Bad settings fail silently.** Only send `cfg_scale` (how closely it follows the description) in `json_config`. An unknown key or a value out of range still returns 201, but the candidates never become ready, so put a time limit on your status checks.
- Converted voices count toward your custom-voice limit. Unconverted candidates expire after 30 days.

For you, that means it suits designing a persona once (or once per user) and caching the `voice_id`. It doesn't suit changing the voice's character mid-conversation. For that, you'd have to switch between several voices you designed in advance.

entries.name: EnterWorktree
entries.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

name.description: Optional name for a new worktree. Each "/"-separated segment may contain only letters, digits, dots, underscores, and dashes; max 64 chars total. A random name is generated if not provided. Mutually exclusive with `path`.

path.description: Path to an existing worktree to switch into instead of creating a new one. Must appear in `git worktree list` for the current repo — or, on first entry from the launch directory, for a repo nested inside it (multi-repo workspace). Mutually exclusive with `name`.

"""Gradium speech in and out, in the wire format of contracts § Audio
(PCM s16le, mono, 24 kHz, base64).

Checks, from backend/:
    uv run python voice.py tts "Hello from the beaver"   # writes out.wav, prints time to first audio
    uv run python voice.py stt out.wav                    # prints the transcript
"""

import asyncio
import base64
import json
import logging
import os
import sys
import time
import wave
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Awaitable, Callable

import certifi

# python.org builds on macOS ship without CA certs. aiohttp (inside gradium) builds its
# TLS context at import time, so this must run before `import gradium`.
os.environ.setdefault("SSL_CERT_FILE", certifi.where())

import aiohttp  # noqa: E402  (gradium's own transport)
import gradium  # noqa: E402

SAMPLE_RATE = 24000
CHUNK_BYTES = 3840  # 80 ms
DEFAULT_VOICE_ID = "JuMRs5W5S52hzuge"  # Cormac: bright, warm, cheerful (flagship catalog)

# Hands-free end of turn, from the semantic VAD in Gradium's `step` messages (one per 80 ms).
END_HORIZON_S = 2.0  # read the `vad` entry with this horizon_s
END_PROB = 0.5  # its inactivity_prob must be above this...
END_STEPS = 3  # ...for this many steps in a row, once the turn has text
REOPEN_AFTER_S = 1.0  # a closed hands-free session reopens on the next audio, at most once a second
BACKLOG_CHUNKS = 25  # hands-free audio waiting for a session: the newest 2 s, older chunks drop

# Gradium keyword boosting for the demo's place names. Case-sensitive, hence the variants.
# Synthetic test voices still say "Bern" like "burn", so the agent also resolves names.
_PLACES = ["Bern", "Zürich", "Zurich", "Basel", "Luzern", "Geneva", "Lausanne"]
KEYWORDS = {"words": _PLACES + [p.lower() for p in _PLACES] + ["SBB"], "boost": 3}

log = logging.getLogger("voice")
_client: gradium.client.GradiumClient | None = None


def client() -> gradium.client.GradiumClient:
    global _client
    if _client is None:
        _client = gradium.client.GradiumClient()  # reads GRADIUM_API_KEY
    return _client


async def speak(text: str) -> AsyncIterator[str]:
    """Yield base64 PCM chunks for `text`. One TTS socket per reply."""
    voice_id = os.environ.get("GRADIUM_VOICE_ID") or DEFAULT_VOICE_ID
    async with client().tts_realtime(
        model_name="default", voice_id=voice_id, output_format="pcm_24000"
    ) as tts:
        await tts.send_text(text)
        await tts.send_eos()
        async for msg in _messages(tts):  # raw frames: base64 audio passes through as is
            if msg["type"] == "audio":
                yield msg["audio"]
            elif msg["type"] == "end_of_stream":
                break


class Transcriber:
    """One push-to-talk turn: push() base64 chunks as they arrive, then finish()."""

    def __init__(self, language: str = "en"):
        self._queue: asyncio.Queue[bytes | None] = asyncio.Queue()
        self._task = asyncio.create_task(self._run(language))

    def push(self, b64: str) -> None:
        self._queue.put_nowait(base64.b64decode(b64))

    async def finish(self) -> str:
        """End of speech: Gradium drains the remaining text, then closes."""
        self._queue.put_nowait(None)
        return await self._task

    def cancel(self) -> None:
        self._task.cancel()

    async def _run(self, language: str) -> str:
        parts: list[str] = []
        async with client().stt_realtime(
            model_name="default", input_format="pcm", json_config={"language": language, "keywords": KEYWORDS}
        ) as stt:

            async def send() -> None:
                while (chunk := await self._queue.get()) is not None:
                    await stt.send_audio(chunk)
                await stt.send_eos()

            sender = asyncio.create_task(send())
            try:
                async for msg in _messages(stt):
                    if msg["type"] == "text":
                        parts.append(msg["text"])
                    elif msg["type"] == "end_of_stream":
                        break
            finally:
                sender.cancel()
        return " ".join(p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip())


async def _messages(stream) -> AsyncIterator[dict]:
    """STT or TTS messages. Use instead of `async for msg in stream`: in gradium 0.6.4 that
    spins forever, freezing the event loop, when the connection drops without a close frame."""
    async for frame in stream._ws:  # aiohttp stops iterating on any close
        if frame.type == aiohttp.WSMsgType.TEXT:
            msg = json.loads(frame.data)
            if msg["type"] == "error":
                raise RuntimeError(f"Gradium error: {msg}")
            yield msg


class TurnDetector:
    """Hands-free end of turn: inactivity_prob at END_HORIZON_S above END_PROB for
    END_STEPS `step`s in a row, counted only once the turn has text."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.words: list[str] = []
        self._streak = 0

    def feed(self, msg: dict) -> bool:
        """One STT message in; True when the turn has ended."""
        if msg["type"] == "text" and msg["text"].strip():
            self.words.append(msg["text"].strip())
        elif msg["type"] == "step" and self.words:
            p = next((v["inactivity_prob"] for v in msg["vad"] if v["horizon_s"] == END_HORIZON_S), 0.0)
            self._streak = self._streak + 1 if p > END_PROB else 0
            return self._streak >= END_STEPS
        return False

    def take(self) -> str:
        """The turn's text; starts the next turn."""
        text, self.words, self._streak = " ".join(self.words), [], 0
        return text


class ContinuousTranscriber:
    """Hands-free: one STT session per WebSocket, open across turns. push() base64 chunks
    for as long as the mic is on. Awaits on_speech() at a turn's first words and
    on_turn(text) at its end. If Gradium closes the session, the next push() reopens it."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        on_speech: Callable[[], Awaitable[None]],
        on_turn: Callable[[str], Awaitable[None]],
        language: str = "en",
    ):
        self._on_speech, self._on_turn, self._language = on_speech, on_turn, language
        self._queue: asyncio.Queue[bytes] = asyncio.Queue(BACKLOG_CHUNKS)
        self._turn = TurnDetector()  # outlives a session, so a turn survives a reopen
        self._task: asyncio.Task | None = None
        self._opened = float("-inf")

    def push(self, b64: str) -> None:
        closed = self._task is None or self._task.done()
        if closed and time.monotonic() - self._opened > REOPEN_AFTER_S:
            self._opened = time.monotonic()
            self._task = asyncio.create_task(self._run())
        if self._queue.full():  # no session drains it: drop the oldest, never replay a stale backlog
            self._queue.get_nowait()
        self._queue.put_nowait(base64.b64decode(b64))

    def cancel(self) -> None:
        if self._task is not None:
            self._task.cancel()

    async def _run(self) -> None:
        try:
            async with client().stt_realtime(
                model_name="default", input_format="pcm", json_config={"language": self._language, "keywords": KEYWORDS}
            ) as stt:

                async def send() -> None:
                    while True:
                        await stt.send_audio(await self._queue.get())

                sender = asyncio.create_task(send())
                try:
                    await self._listen(stt)
                finally:
                    sender.cancel()
        except Exception:
            log.exception("hands-free STT failed")
        log.info("hands-free STT session closed; the next audio reopens it")

    async def _listen(self, stt) -> None:
        # A flush sent on a closed session gets no `flushed`; an ended turn flushes again on the next `step`.
        turn, flushing = self._turn, False
        async for msg in _messages(stt):
            fresh = not turn.words
            ended = turn.feed(msg)
            if fresh and turn.words:
                await self._on_speech()
            if ended and not flushing:  # flush makes Gradium emit the words it holds back
                flushing = True
                await stt.send_flush()
            elif msg["type"] == "flushed" and flushing:
                flushing = False
                await self._on_turn(turn.take())


async def _cli_tts(text: str) -> None:
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    first = None
    pcm = bytearray()
    async for chunk in speak(text):
        first = first or time.monotonic() - t0
        pcm += base64.b64decode(chunk)
    with wave.open("out.wav", "wb") as f:
        f.setnchannels(1)
        f.setsampwidth(2)
        f.setframerate(SAMPLE_RATE)
        f.writeframes(bytes(pcm))
    print(f"out.wav: {len(pcm) / 2 / SAMPLE_RATE:.2f} s audio, first audio after {first:.2f} s")


async def _cli_stt(path: str) -> None:
    with wave.open(path, "rb") as f:
        assert (f.getframerate(), f.getnchannels(), f.getsampwidth()) == (SAMPLE_RATE, 1, 2), "need 24 kHz mono s16"
        pcm = f.readframes(f.getnframes())
    stt = Transcriber()
    for i in range(0, len(pcm), CHUNK_BYTES):  # paced like a live mic
        stt.push(base64.b64encode(pcm[i : i + CHUNK_BYTES]).decode())
        await asyncio.sleep(0.08)
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    text = await stt.finish()
    print(f"transcript ({time.monotonic() - t0:.2f} s after end of audio): {text!r}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from dotenv import load_dotenv

    load_dotenv()
    load_dotenv("../.env")
    cmd, arg = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    asyncio.run(_cli_tts(arg) if cmd == "tts" else _cli_stt(arg))

"""FastAPI server: the app's WebSocket, the screenshot endpoint, and turn orchestration.

Protocol and interfaces: docs/contracts.md. Run from backend/:
    uv run uvicorn app:app --reload --port 8000
"""

import asyncio
import base64
import contextlib
import hmac
import inspect
import json
import logging
import os
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from dotenv import load_dotenv
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Request, Response, WebSocket, WebSocketDisconnect
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse

import voice

HERE = Path(__file__).parent
load_dotenv(HERE / ".env")
load_dotenv(HERE.parent / ".env")
FIXTURES = HERE / "fixtures"

log = logging.getLogger("app")
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(name)s %(message)s")

try:  # WP3 ships a2ui.py; until then we send `reply` only.
    from a2ui import cards_to_a2ui
except ImportError:
    cards_to_a2ui = None

try:  # vision.py is written in parallel; without it every screenshot reads as None.
    from vision import read_screen
except ImportError:
    read_screen = None

SCREEN_MIMES = {"image/jpeg", "image/png"}
SCREEN_MAX_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024
SCREEN_MAX_AGE = 120  # s; contracts § HTTP, screenshot rule
VISION_WAIT = 5  # s a turn waits for a running vision call


@dataclass
class Screenshot:
    id: int
    image: bytes
    mime: str
    at: float  # time.monotonic() when received
    task: asyncio.Task | None = None  # read_screen in the background; its result is the ScreenContext
    used: bool = False


# Single user: one latest screenshot, shared by all sessions.
latest: Screenshot | None = None
sessions: set["Session"] = set()


class StubAgent:
    """Same shape as WP3's Agent (contracts § Agent interface)."""

    async def start(self) -> None:
        pass

    async def turn(self, text, screen, on_status):
        await on_status("Checking trains…")
        await asyncio.sleep(1)
        return json.loads((FIXTURES / "demo_reply.json").read_text())


def make_agent():
    if os.environ.get("MOCK_AGENT", "1") != "1":
        try:
            from agent import Agent

            return Agent()
        except ImportError:
            pass
        try:  # prototype stand-in until WP3's agent.py lands
            from dev_agent import DevAgent

            log.info("agent.py not available yet, using DevAgent")
            return DevAgent()
        except ImportError:
            log.warning("no agent.py or dev_agent.py, using StubAgent")
    return StubAgent()


def token_ok(token: object) -> bool:
    expected = os.environ.get("APP_TOKEN", "")
    return bool(expected) and isinstance(token, str) and hmac.compare_digest(token, expected)


async def broadcast(msg: dict) -> None:
    for session in list(sessions):
        try:
            await session.send(msg)
        except Exception:
            log.warning("could not send %s to a session", msg["type"])


async def read_latest(shot: Screenshot) -> dict | None:
    """Run vision on one screenshot, tell every session, return its ScreenContext or None."""
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    screen = None
    if read_screen is None:
        log.warning("vision.py not available, screenshot %d not read", shot.id)
    else:
        try:
            if inspect.iscoroutinefunction(read_screen):
                screen = await read_screen(shot.image, shot.mime)
            else:  # a sync read_screen must not block the event loop
                screen = await asyncio.to_thread(read_screen, shot.image, shot.mime)
        except Exception:
            log.exception("vision failed on screenshot %d", shot.id)
        screen = screen if isinstance(screen, dict) else None
    summary = screen.get("summary") if screen else None
    log.info("screenshot %d read in %.2fs: %r", shot.id, time.monotonic() - t0, summary)
    await broadcast({"type": "screen_ok"} | ({"summary": summary} if summary else {}))
    return screen


def store_screenshot(image: bytes, mime: str) -> None:
    """Keep only the latest screenshot and start reading it."""
    global latest
    if latest and latest.task:
        latest.task.cancel()  # its context is stale now
    latest = Screenshot(latest.id + 1 if latest else 1, image, mime, time.monotonic())
    latest.task = asyncio.create_task(read_latest(latest))
    log.info("screenshot %d: %d bytes %s", latest.id, len(image), mime)


async def take_screen() -> tuple[Screenshot | None, dict | None]:
    """The latest screenshot and its ScreenContext if fresh and unused (contracts § HTTP).

    The caller marks it used once its turn completes, so a turn the user interrupts
    leaves the screen for the question they ask next."""
    deadline = time.monotonic() + VISION_WAIT
    while True:
        shot = latest
        if shot is None or shot.used or time.monotonic() - shot.at > SCREEN_MAX_AGE:
            return None, None
        await asyncio.wait({shot.task}, timeout=max(0, deadline - time.monotonic()))  # never cancels the vision task
        if shot is latest or not shot.task.cancelled():
            break  # else a newer screenshot cancelled it: wait on that one, same deadline
    if not shot.task.done() or shot.task.cancelled():
        log.warning("screenshot %d not read within %ds, turn goes without it", shot.id, VISION_WAIT)
        return None, None
    return shot, shot.task.result()


app = FastAPI()


@app.get("/")
async def prototype_client():
    """Mac prototype client (static/index.html); the iPhone app doesn't use it."""
    return FileResponse(HERE / "static" / "index.html")


@app.get("/health")
async def health():
    return {"ok": True, "workspace": os.environ.get("WORKSPACE_MODE", "fixture")}


@app.post("/screenshot", status_code=204)
async def screenshot(request: Request) -> Response:

    if mime not in SCREEN_MIMES:
        raise HTTPException(415)
    image = bytearray()
    async for chunk in request.stream():  # count bytes; Content-Length can lie
        image += chunk
        if len(image) > SCREEN_MAX_BYTES:
            raise HTTPException(413)
    store_screenshot(bytes(image), mime)
    return Response(status_code=204)

    def __init__(self, ws: WebSocket, handsfree: bool = False):
        self.ws = ws
        self.agent = make_agent()
        self.turns = 0
        self.stt: voice.Transcriber | None = None
        self.listener = voice.ContinuousTranscriber(self.heard_speech, self.heard_turn) if handsfree else None
        self.turn_task: asyncio.Task | None = None
        self._send_lock = asyncio.Lock()

    async def send(self, msg: dict) -> None:
        async with self._send_lock:
            await self.ws.send_json(msg)

    async def state(self, state: str, label: str | None = None) -> None:
        await self.send({"type": "state", "state": state} | ({"label": label} if label else {}))

    async def run_turn(self, text: str, timings: dict[str, float] | None = None) -> None:
        self.turns += 1
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        timings = timings or {}
        await self.state("thinking")

        async def on_status(label: str) -> None:
            await self.state("searching", label)

        shot, screen = await take_screen()
        timings["vision_wait"] = time.monotonic() - t0
        t_agent = time.monotonic()
        try:
            reply = await self.agent.turn(text, screen, on_status)
        except Exception:
            log.exception("turn failed")
            await self.send({"type": "error", "message": "Sorry, something went wrong."})
            await self.state("idle")
            return
        timings["agent"] = time.monotonic() - t_agent
        if shot is not None:
            shot.used = True

        await self.send({"type": "reply", "say": reply["say"], "cards": reply["cards"]})
        if cards_to_a2ui and reply["cards"]:
            messages = cards_to_a2ui(f"reply-{self.turns}", reply["cards"])
            await self.send({"type": "a2ui", "messages": messages})
        await self.state("speaking")
        try:  # aclosing: an interrupt closes the TTS socket now, not when GC finds it
            async with contextlib.aclosing(voice.speak(reply["say"])) as chunks:
                async for chunk in chunks:
                    timings.setdefault("first_audio", time.monotonic() - t0)
                    await self.send({"type": "audio", "data": chunk})
        except Exception:
            log.exception("TTS failed")  # the reply text and cards are already on screen
        await self.send({"type": "audio_end"})
        await self.state("idle")
        timings["total"] = time.monotonic() - t0
        log.info("turn %d %r timings %s", self.turns, text, {k: round(v, 2) for k, v in timings.items()})

    async def voice_turn(self, stt: voice.Transcriber) -> None:
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        try:
            text = await stt.finish()
        except Exception:
            log.exception("STT failed")
            text = ""
        if not text:
            await self.send({"type": "error", "message": "Sorry, I didn't catch that."})
            await self.state("idle")
            return
        await self.send({"type": "transcript", "text": text})
        await self.run_turn(text, {"stt": time.monotonic() - t0})

    async def heard_speech(self) -> None:
        """Hands-free: the user's first words of a turn; talking over the mascot interrupts it."""
        await self.interrupt()
        await self.state("listening")

    async def heard_turn(self, text: str) -> None:
        """Hands-free: Gradium's VAD says the user is done."""
        await self.interrupt()
        await self.send({"type": "transcript", "text": text})
        await self.start_turn(self.run_turn(text))

    async def start_turn(self, coro) -> None:
        """One turn at a time: cancel the running one first. Turns run as tasks so the
        receive loop can still hear an interrupt."""
        await self.interrupt()
        self.turn_task = asyncio.create_task(coro)

    async def interrupt(self) -> bool:
        """Cancel the running turn: the agent call and the TTS socket. True if one was running."""
        task, self.turn_task = self.turn_task, None
        if task is None or task.done():
            return False
        task.cancel()
        try:
            await task
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            pass
        log.info("turn %d interrupted", self.turns)
        return True

    async def handle(self, msg: dict) -> None:
        kind = msg.get("type")
        if kind == "audio" and self.listener is not None and isinstance(msg.get("data"), str):
            self.listener.push(msg["data"])  # hands-free: the mic never stops, no audio_end
        elif kind == "audio" and isinstance(msg.get("data"), str):
            if self.stt is None:  # a new press; talking over the mascot interrupts it
                await self.interrupt()
                self.stt = voice.Transcriber()
                await self.state("listening")
            self.stt.push(msg["data"])
        elif kind == "audio_end" and self.stt is not None:
            stt, self.stt = self.stt, None
            await self.start_turn(self.voice_turn(stt))
        elif kind == "text" and isinstance(msg.get("text"), str):
            await self.start_turn(self.run_turn(msg["text"]))
        elif kind == "screen":
            try:
                image = base64.b64decode(msg.get("data"), validate=True)
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                image = b""
            if msg.get("mime") in SCREEN_MIMES and 0 < len(image) <= SCREEN_MAX_BYTES:
                store_screenshot(image, msg["mime"])
            else:
                log.warning("ignored screen frame: bad mime, base64 or size")
        elif kind == "interrupt":
            if await self.interrupt():
                await self.state("idle")
        else:
            log.warning("ignored message type %r", kind)

    def close(self) -> None:
        if self.stt is not None:
            self.stt.cancel()
        if self.listener is not None:
            self.listener.cancel()
        if self.turn_task is not None:
            self.turn_task.cancel()


@app.websocket("/ws")
async def ws_endpoint(ws: WebSocket):
    await ws.accept()
    # A malformed frame: bad JSON (ValueError), a binary frame (KeyError), bad base64 (ValueError).
    # Not RuntimeError: Starlette raises it on every receive once the socket is gone.
    bad_frame = (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError)
    try:
        try:
            hello = await ws.receive_json()
        except bad_frame:
            hello = None
        if not isinstance(hello, dict) or hello.get("type") != "hello" or not token_ok(hello.get("token")):
            await ws.close(code=1008)
            return
        session = Session(ws, handsfree=hello.get("mode") == "handsfree")
        await session.agent.start()
        await session.send({"type": "ready"})
        sessions.add(session)
        try:
            while True:
                try:
                    msg = await ws.receive_json()
                    if isinstance(msg, dict):
                        await session.handle(msg)
                except bad_frame as e:
                    log.warning("ignored malformed frame: %r", e)
        finally:
            sessions.discard(session)
            session.close()
    except WebSocketDisconnect:
        pass

            await self.send({"type": "a2ui", "messages": messages})

            log.exception("TTS failed")  # the reply text and cards are already on screen
        await self.send({"type": "audio_end"})
        await self.state("idle")

        log.info("turn %d %r timings %s", self.turns, text, {k: round(v, 2) for k, v in timings.items()})

    async def voice_turn(self, stt: voice.Transcriber) -> None:
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        try:
            text = await stt.finish()
        except Exception:

            text = ""

            await self.send({"type": "error", "message": "Sorry, I didn't catch that."})

        await self.interrupt()

        task.cancel()
        try:

        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            pass

        kind = msg.get("type")

            self.listener.push(msg["data"])  # hands-free: the mic never stops, no audio_end

            self.stt.push(msg["data"])
        elif kind == "audio_end" and self.stt is not None:
            stt, self.stt = self.stt, None
            await self.start_turn(self.voice_turn(stt))
        elif kind == "text" and isinstance(msg.get("text"), str):
            await self.start_turn(self.run_turn(msg["text"]))
        elif kind == "screen":
            try:
                image = base64.b64decode(msg.get("data"), validate=True)
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                image = b""
            if msg.get("mime") in SCREEN_MIMES and 0 < len(image) <= SCREEN_MAX_BYTES:
                store_screenshot(image, msg["mime"])
            else:
                log.warning("ignored screen frame: bad mime, base64 or size")
        elif kind == "interrupt":
            if await self.interrupt():
                await self.state("idle")
        else:
            log.warning("ignored message type %r", kind)

    def close(self) -> None:
        if self.stt is not None:
            self.stt.cancel()
        if self.listener is not None:
            self.listener.cancel()
        if self.turn_task is not None:

async def ws_endpoint(ws: WebSocket):
    await ws.accept()
    # A malformed frame: bad JSON (ValueError), a binary frame (KeyError), bad base64 (ValueError).
    # Not RuntimeError: Starlette raises it on every receive once the socket is gone.
    bad_frame = (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError)
    try:
        try:
            hello = await ws.receive_json()
        except bad_frame:
            hello = None
        if not isinstance(hello, dict) or hello.get("type") != "hello" or not token_ok(hello.get("token")):
            await ws.close(code=1008)
            return
        session = Session(ws, handsfree=hello.get("mode") == "handsfree")
        await session.agent.start()
        await session.send({"type": "ready"})
        sessions.add(session)
        try:
            while True:
                try:
                    msg = await ws.receive_json()
                    if isinstance(msg, dict):
                        await session.handle(msg)
                except bad_frame as e:
                    log.warning("ignored malformed frame: %r", e)
        finally:
            sessions.discard(session)
            session.close()

def schema_error(value, schema: dict, at: str) -> str | None:
    """Check value against the JSON Schema subset used above; return the first problem or None.

    Optional fields may be missing or null."""
    if "anyOf" in schema:
        kind = value.get("kind") if isinstance(value, dict) else None
        branch = next((s for s in schema["anyOf"] if s["properties"]["kind"]["enum"] == [kind]), None)
        return schema_error(value, branch, at) if branch else f"{at}.kind must be train, conflict, event or flight"
    expected = schema["type"]
    if expected == "object":
        if not isinstance(value, dict):
            return f"{at} must be an object"
        for key, sub in schema["properties"].items():
            if value.get(key) is None:
                if key in schema["required"]:
                    return f"{at}.{key} is missing"
            elif error := schema_error(value[key], sub, f"{at}.{key}"):
                return error
        return None
    if expected == "array":
        if not isinstance(value, list) or len(value) > schema["maxItems"]:
            return f"{at} must be a list of at most {schema['maxItems']}"
        return next((e for i, v in enumerate(value) if (e := schema_error(v, schema["items"], f"{at}[{i}]"))), None)
    if not isinstance(value, {"string": str, "integer": int}[expected]) or isinstance(value, bool):
        return f"{at} must be a {expected}"
    if value not in schema.get("enum", [value]):
        return f"{at} must be one of {schema['enum']}"
    if schema.get("format") == "date-time" and not _parses(value, ISO, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z"):
        return f"{at} must be ISO 8601 with offset, e.g. 2026-10-15T18:01:00+02:00"
    return None


async def sbb_connections(from_station: str, to_station: str, depart_after: str) -> dict:
    when = datetime.fromisoformat(depart_after)
    when = when.astimezone(TZ) if when.tzinfo else when.replace(tzinfo=TZ)
    params = {"from": from_station, "to": to_station, "date": f"{when:%Y-%m-%d}", "time": f"{when:%H:%M}", "limit": 4}
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=4) as http:
        r = await http.get(SBB_URL, params=params)
        r.raise_for_status()
    return compact(r.json())


def compact(data: dict) -> dict:

class DevAgent:
    async def start(self) -> None:
        context = CONTEXT.read_text()
        self.events = json.loads(context).get("events", [])
        self.prompt = f"{PROMPT}\n\n<context>\nCalendar from now to 7 days ahead, and flight emails:\n{context}</context>"
        self.history: list[list[types.Content]] = []  # one list of contents per completed turn

    async def turn(self, text, screen, on_status) -> dict:
        try:
            return await self._turn(text, screen, on_status)
        except Exception:  # CancelledError is a BaseException, so interrupts still propagate
            log.exception("turn failed")
            return {"say": SORRY, "cards": []}

    async def _turn(self, text, screen, on_status) -> dict:
        now = datetime.now(TZ)
        parts = [types.Part(text=text)]
        if screen:
            screen_json = json.dumps(screen, ensure_ascii=False)
            parts.insert(0, types.Part(text=f"<screen_context>\n{screen_json}\n</screen_context>"))
            if trains := await self._prefetch_trains(screen, now, on_status):
                parts.insert(1, types.Part(text=f"<trains>\n{json.dumps(trains, ensure_ascii=False)}\n</trains>"))
        new = [types.Content(role="user", parts=parts)]  # this turn; joins the history once it completes
        past = [content for turn in self.history for content in turn]
        retried = False
        for step in range(MAX_STEPS):
            last = step == MAX_STEPS - 1
            t0 = time.monotonic()
            response = await client().aio.models.generate_content(
                model=os.environ.get("GEMINI_MODEL") or DEFAULT_MODEL,
                contents=past + new,
                config=self._config(now, last),
            )
            content = response.candidates[0].content
            calls = [p.function_call for p in content.parts or [] if p.function_call]
            usage = response.usage_metadata
            log.info(
                "step %d took %.2f s: %s, tokens in %s, thinking %s, out %s",
                step, time.monotonic() - t0, [c.name for c in calls],
                usage and usage.prompt_token_count, usage and usage.thoughts_token_count,
                usage and usage.candidates_token_count,
            )  # fmt: skip
            if not calls:
                raise ValueError("model answered without a function call")
            new.append(content)  # unmodified: it carries the thought signatures

            respond = next((c for c in calls if c.name == "respond"), None)
            skipped = {"error": "not run, the turn ended with respond"}
            if respond is None:
                if any(c.name == "sbb_connections" for c in calls):
                    await on_status("Checking trains…")
                results = await asyncio.gather(*(self._run(c) for c in calls))
            elif (error := schema_error(respond.args, RESPOND, "respond")) and not retried and not last:
                retried = True
                log.warning("invalid respond, retrying: %s", error)
                results = [{"error": f"{error}. Call respond again."} if c is respond else skipped for c in calls]
            else:
                if error:
                    log.warning("invalid respond again, replying without cards: %s", error)
                new.append(_responses(calls, [{"ok": True} if c is respond else skipped for c in calls]))
                self.history = (self.history + [new])[-MAX_TURNS:]
                say = respond.args.get("say") if isinstance(respond.args, dict) else None
                if not isinstance(say, str) or not say:
                    return {"say": SORRY, "cards": []}
                return {"say": say, "cards": [] if error else respond.args["cards"]}
            new.append(_responses(calls, results))
        raise ValueError(f"no respond in {MAX_STEPS} steps")

    def _config(self, now: datetime, last: bool) -> types.GenerateContentConfig:
        return types.GenerateContentConfig(
            system_instruction=f"{self.prompt}\n\nNow: {now:%A %Y-%m-%d %H:%M} (Europe/Zurich).",
            tools=[TOOLS],
            tool_config=types.ToolConfig(
                function_calling_config=types.FunctionCallingConfig(
                    mode=types.FunctionCallingConfigMode.ANY,
                    allowed_function_names=["respond"] if last else None,
                )
            ),
            thinking_config=types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_level=types.ThinkingLevel.LOW),
            automatic_function_calling=types.AutomaticFunctionCallingConfig(disable=True),
        )

    async def _prefetch_trains(self, screen: dict, now: datetime, on_status) -> dict | None:
        """The lookup the model would ask for first, done before the model call: trains to the
        plan on screen, after the last event that ends before it (+ the walk). Saves one model
        step, about 3-4 s. None when there's no out-of-town plan with a date and time."""
        p = screen.get("proposal") or {}
        place, date, hm = p.get("place"), p.get("date"), p.get("time")
        if not (isinstance(place, str) and date and hm) or place.lower() in ("zürich", "zurich"):
            return None
        try:
            start = datetime.fromisoformat(f"{date}T{hm}").replace(tzinfo=TZ)
        except ValueError:
            return None
        ends = [
            end for e in self.events
            if (end := datetime.fromisoformat(e["end"])) <= start and end.date() == start.date()
        ]  # fmt: skip
        after = max(ends) + WALK if ends else start - timedelta(hours=2)
        after = max(after, now + WALK)
        args = {"from_station": HOME_STATION, "to_station": place, "depart_after": after.isoformat()}
        await on_status("Checking trains…")
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        try:
            result = await sbb_connections(**args)
        except Exception as e:
            log.warning("train prefetch %s failed: %r", args, e)
            return None
        log.info("train prefetch %s took %.2f s", args, time.monotonic() - t0)
        return {"query": args, **result}

    async def _run(self, call: types.FunctionCall) -> dict:
        """Tool errors go back to the model, which can tell the user; they never end the turn."""
        if call.name != "sbb_connections":
            return {"error": f"unknown function {call.name}"}
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        try:
            result = await sbb_connections(**(call.args or {}))
        except Exception as e:
            log.warning("sbb_connections %s failed: %r", call.args, e)
            return {"error": f"timetable lookup failed: {type(e).__name__}"}
        log.info("sbb_connections %s took %.2f s", call.args, time.monotonic() - t0)
        return result


def _responses(calls: list[types.FunctionCall], results: list[dict]) -> types.Content:
    """One function response per call, with the call's id and name."""
    parts = [
        types.Part(function_response=types.FunctionResponse(id=c.id, name=c.name, response=r))
        for c, r in zip(calls, results)
    ]
    return types.Content(role="user", parts=parts)


async def _cli(question: str, screen_path: str | None) -> None:
    agent = DevAgent()
    await agent.start()
    screen = json.loads(Path(screen_path).read_text()) if screen_path else None

    async def on_status(label: str) -> None:
        log.info("status: %s", label)

    t0 = time.monotonic()
    reply = await agent.turn(question, screen, on_status)
    print(json.dumps(reply, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    print(f"took {time.monotonic() - t0:.2f} s")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from dotenv import load_dotenv

    load_dotenv()
    load_dotenv("../.env")
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(name)s %(message)s")
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("question")
    parser.add_argument("--screen", help="a ScreenContext JSON file, e.g. fixtures/screen.json")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    asyncio.run(_cli(args.question, args.screen))

                "arrival_platform": c["to"]["platform"],
                "transfers": c["transfers"],
                "delay_min": c["from"]["delay"] or 0,  # null: no realtime data yet
                "duration_min": (arr - dep) // 60,
            }
        )
    return {"connections": out}


class DevAgent:
    async def start(self) -> None:
        context = CONTEXT.read_text()
        self.events = json.loads(context).get("events", [])
        self.prompt = f"{PROMPT}\n\n<context>\nCalendar from now to 7 days ahead, and flight emails:\n{context}</context>"
        self.history: list[list[types.Content]] = []  # one list of contents per completed turn

    async def turn(self, text, screen, on_status) -> dict:
        try:
            return await self._turn(text, screen, on_status)
        except Exception:  # CancelledError is a BaseException, so interrupts still propagate
            log.exception("turn failed")
            return {"say": SORRY, "cards": []}

    async def _turn(self, text, screen, on_status) -> dict:
        now = datetime.now(TZ)
        parts = [types.Part(text=text)]
        if screen:
            screen_json = json.dumps(screen, ensure_ascii=False)
            parts.insert(0, types.Part(text=f"<screen_context>\n{screen_json}\n</screen_context>"))
            if trains := await self._prefetch_trains(screen, now, on_status):
                parts.insert(1, types.Part(text=f"<trains>\n{json.dumps(trains, ensure_ascii=False)}\n</trains>"))
        new = [types.Content(role="user", parts=parts)]  # this turn; joins the history once it completes
        past = [content for turn in self.history for content in turn]
        retried = False
        for step in range(MAX_STEPS):
            last = step == MAX_STEPS - 1
            t0 = time.monotonic()
            response = await client().aio.models.generate_content(
                model=os.environ.get("GEMINI_MODEL") or DEFAULT_MODEL,
                contents=past + new,
                config=self._config(now, last),
            )
            content = response.candidates[0].content
            calls = [p.function_call for p in content.parts or [] if p.function_call]
            usage = response.usage_metadata
            log.info(
                "step %d took %.2f s: %s, tokens in %s, thinking %s, out %s",
                step, time.monotonic() - t0, [c.name for c in calls],
                usage and usage.prompt_token_count, usage and usage.thoughts_token_count,
                usage and usage.candidates_token_count,
            )  # fmt: skip
            if not calls:
                raise ValueError("model answered without a function call")
            new.append(content)  # unmodified: it carries the thought signatures

            respond = next((c for c in calls if c.name == "respond"), None)
            skipped = {"error": "not run, the turn ended with respond"}
            if respond is None:
                if any(c.name == "sbb_connections" for c in calls):
                    await on_status("Checking trains…")
                results = await asyncio.gather(*(self._run(c) for c in calls))
            elif (error := schema_error(respond.args, RESPOND, "respond")) and not retried and not last:
                retried = True
                log.warning("invalid respond, retrying: %s", error)
                results = [{"error": f"{error}. Call respond again."} if c is respond else skipped for c in calls]
            else:
                if error:
                    log.warning("invalid respond again, replying without cards: %s", error)
                new.append(_responses(calls, [{"ok": True} if c is respond else skipped for c in calls]))
                self.history = (self.history + [new])[-MAX_TURNS:]
                say = respond.args.get("say") if isinstance(respond.args, dict) else None
                if not isinstance(say, str) or not say:
                    return {"say": SORRY, "cards": []}
                return {"say": say, "cards": [] if error else respond.args["cards"]}
            new.append(_responses(calls, results))
        raise ValueError(f"no respond in {MAX_STEPS} steps")

    def _config(self, now: datetime, last: bool) -> types.GenerateContentConfig:
        return types.GenerateContentConfig(
            system_instruction=f"{self.prompt}\n\nNow: {now:%A %Y-%m-%d %H:%M} (Europe/Zurich).",
            tools=[TOOLS],
            tool_config=types.ToolConfig(
                function_calling_config=types.FunctionCallingConfig(
                    mode=types.FunctionCallingConfigMode.ANY,
                    allowed_function_names=["respond"] if last else None,
                )
            ),
            thinking_config=types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_level=types.ThinkingLevel.LOW),
            automatic_function_calling=types.AutomaticFunctionCallingConfig(disable=True),
        )

    async def _prefetch_trains(self, screen: dict, now: datetime, on_status) -> dict | None:
        """The lookup the model would ask for first, done before the model call: trains to the
        plan on screen, after the last event that ends before it (+ the walk). Saves one model
        step, about 3-4 s. None when there's no out-of-town plan with a date and time."""
        p = screen.get("proposal") or {}
        place, date, hm = p.get("place"), p.get("date"), p.get("time")
        if not (isinstance(place, str) and date and hm) or place.lower() in ("zürich", "zurich"):
            return None
        try:
            start = datetime.fromisoformat(f"{date}T{hm}").replace(tzinfo=TZ)
        except ValueError:
            return None
        ends = [
            end for e in self.events
            if (end := datetime.fromisoformat(e["end"])) <= start and end.date() == start.date()
        ]  # fmt: skip
        after = max(ends) + WALK if ends else start - timedelta(hours=2)
        after = max(after, now + WALK)
        args = {"from_station": HOME_STATION, "to_station": place, "depart_after": after.isoformat()}
        await on_status("Checking trains…")
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        try:
            result = await sbb_connections(**args)
        except Exception as e:
            log.warning("train prefetch %s failed: %r", args, e)
            return None
        log.info("train prefetch %s took %.2f s", args, time.monotonic() - t0)
        return {"query": args, **result}

    async def _run(self, call: types.FunctionCall) -> dict:
        """Tool errors go back to the model, which can tell the user; they never end the turn."""
        if call.name != "sbb_connections":
            return {"error": f"unknown function {call.name}"}
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        try:
            result = await sbb_connections(**(call.args or {}))
        except Exception as e:
            log.warning("sbb_connections %s failed: %r", call.args, e)
            return {"error": f"timetable lookup failed: {type(e).__name__}"}
        log.info("sbb_connections %s took %.2f s", call.args, time.monotonic() - t0)
        return result


def _responses(calls: list[types.FunctionCall], results: list[dict]) -> types.Content:
    """One function response per call, with the call's id and name."""
    parts = [
        types.Part(function_response=types.FunctionResponse(id=c.id, name=c.name, response=r))
        for c, r in zip(calls, results)
    ]
    return types.Content(role="user", parts=parts)


async def _cli(question: str, screen_path: str | None) -> None:
    agent = DevAgent()
    await agent.start()
    screen = json.loads(Path(screen_path).read_text()) if screen_path else None

    async def on_status(label: str) -> None:
        log.info("status: %s", label)

    t0 = time.monotonic()
    reply = await agent.turn(question, screen, on_status)
    print(json.dumps(reply, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    print(f"took {time.monotonic() - t0:.2f} s")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from dotenv import load_dotenv

    load_dotenv()
    load_dotenv("../.env")
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(name)s %(message)s")
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("question")
    parser.add_argument("--screen", help="a ScreenContext JSON file, e.g. fixtures/screen.json")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    asyncio.run(_cli(args.question, args.screen))

content.content:
<Step title="Wait for them to be ready">
    <CodeGroup>
      ```bash cURL theme={null}
      until curl -s -H "x-api-key: $GRADIUM_API_KEY" \
          "https://api.gradium.ai/api/voice-generator/embeddings?embedding_id=$CAND0" \
          | jq -e '.embeddings[0].ready' > /dev/null; do
        sleep 2
      done
      ```

      ```python Python theme={null}
      import time

      def wait_until_ready(embedding_id, timeout_s=120):
          deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout_s
          while time.monotonic() < deadline:
              resp = requests.get(
                  f"{BASE}/voice-generator/embeddings",
                  params={"embedding_id": embedding_id},
                  headers={"x-api-key": API_KEY},
              )
              resp.raise_for_status()
              found = resp.json()["embeddings"]
              if found and found[0]["ready"]:
                  return found[0]
              time.sleep(2)
          raise TimeoutError(embedding_id)

      for embedding_id in candidates:
          wait_until_ready(embedding_id)
      ```
    </CodeGroup>

    ```json 200 OK theme={null}
    {
      "embeddings": [{
        "embedding_id": "vox_emb_njsiEgpj5NjHKdZc",
        "ready": true,
        "prompt": "A British female voice, 20 to 30, ...",
        "language": "en",
        "created_at": "2026-09-03T11:00:00.968734",
        "expires_at": "2026-10-03T11:00:00.959626"
      }]
    }
    ```

    Three candidates typically take three to five seconds. Bound the loop at
    about two minutes and offer a retry.

    An unknown id returns `200` with an empty `embeddings` list, not `404`, so
    check the list before indexing into it. Timestamps are UTC with or without a
    trailing `Z`.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Listen to a candidate">
    Pass the candidate id as `voice_id` on the normal Text-to-Speech endpoint. The
    `vox_emb_` prefix is how the API tells a candidate from a converted voice.

    <CodeGroup>
      ```bash cURL theme={null}
      curl -s -X POST https://api.gradium.ai/api/post/speech/tts \
        -H "x-api-key: $GRADIUM_API_KEY" \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d "{
          \"text\": \"Hi there, thanks so much for calling! How can I help you today?\",
          \"voice_id\": \"$CAND0\",
          \"model_name\": \"default\",
          \"output_format\": \"wav\",
          \"only_audio\": true
        }" --output candidate-0.wav
      ```

      ```python Python theme={null}
      resp = requests.post(
          f"{BASE}/post/speech/tts",
          json={
              "text": "Hi there, thanks so much for calling! How can I help you today?",
              "voice_id": candidates[0],
              "model_name": "default",
              "output_format": "wav",
              "only_audio": True,
          },
          headers={"x-api-key": API_KEY},
      )
      resp.raise_for_status()
      with open("candidate-0.wav", "wb") as f:
          f.write(resp.content)
      ```
    </CodeGroup>

    The response body is the audio, 48 kHz mono. Repeat for the other candidates.

    Candidates have three restrictions that converted voices do not:

    * Text is capped at 100 characters (`400 input text too long`).
    * REST only. The TTS WebSocket and Speech-to-Speech reject candidate ids with error `1011`.
    * A candidate that is not ready, unknown, or from another account returns `404 Embedding not found`.

    <Tip>
      Audition with the `model_name` and `json_config` you will ship, so the voice
      you approve is the voice you get.
    </Tip>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Convert the candidate into a voice">
    A candidate is a draft, deleted 30 days after generation. Converting it
    creates a permanent voice in your library.

    <CodeGroup>
      ```bash cURL theme={null}
      curl -s -X POST https://api.gradium.ai/api/voices/from-embedding \
        -H "x-api-key: $GRADIUM_API_KEY" \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d "{
          \"voxium_embedding_id\": \"$CAND0\",
          \"name\": \"Receptionist EN\",
          \"description\": \"Front desk and appointment booking\"
        }" > voice.json

      VOICE=$(jq -r '.uid' voice.json)
      ```

      ```python Python theme={null}
      resp = requests.post(
          f"{BASE}/voices/from-embedding",
          json={
              "voxium_embedding_id": candidates[0],
              "name": "Receptionist EN",
              "description": "Front desk and appointment booking",
          },
          headers={"x-api-key": API_KEY},
      )
      resp.raise_for_status()
      voice_id = resp.json()["uid"]
      ```
    </CodeGroup>

    ```json 201 Created theme={null}
    {
      "uid": "b0ntuVzgFdUGoSPc",
      "name": "Receptionist EN",
      "description": "Front desk and appointment booking",
      "filename": "vox_emb_njsiEgpj5NjHKdZc",
      "start_s": 0.0,
      "is_catalog": false,
      "is_pro_clone": false,
      "language": "en",
      "tags": []
    }
    ```

    `uid` is your permanent `voice_id`. Store this one. It is the same value as
    `voxium_embedding_id` in the request and `voice_id` everywhere else.

    * Converting is free. The voice uses one custom-voice slot, shared with [voice clones](/guides/voices/custom-voices). Over the allowance: `409 Custom voice limit reached`.
    * It clears the candidate's expiry.
    * Converting the same candidate twice: `409 A voice was already created from this embedding: <voice_id>`. Store the candidate-to-voice mapping yourself rather than parsing this.
    * Not ready or unknown: `409 Embedding is not ready yet`.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Use the voice">
    <CodeGroup>
      ```bash cURL theme={null}
      curl -s -X POST https://api.gradium.ai/api/post/speech/tts \
        -H "x-api-key: $GRADIUM_API_KEY" \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d "{
          \"text\": \"Good morning, and welcome to Northgate! Do you have an appointment with us today, or shall I get you booked in?\",
          \"voice_id\": \"$VOICE\",
          \"model_name\": \"default\",
          \"output_format\": \"wav\",
          \"only_audio\": true
        }" --output line-0.wav
      ```

      ```python Python theme={null}
      resp = requests.post(
          f"{BASE}/post/speech/tts",
          json={
              "text": (
                  "Good morning, and welcome to Northgate! Do you have an appointment "
                  "with us today, or shall I get you booked in?"
              ),
              "voice_id": voice_id,
              "model_name": "default",
              "output_format": "wav",
              "only_audio": True,
          },
          headers={"x-api-key": API_KEY},
      )
      resp.raise_for_status()
      with open("line-0.wav", "wb") as f:
          f.write(resp.content)
      ```
    </CodeGroup>

    No length cap here. The same `voice_id` works with the
    [Python SDK](/guides/text-to-speech), the
    [TTS WebSocket](/api-reference/endpoint/tts-websocket) and
    [Speech-to-Speech](/guides/speech-to-speech).
  </Step>

  <Step title="Clean up">
    Candidates you do not convert are removed after 30 days. To remove one sooner:

    ```bash cURL theme={null}
    curl -s -X DELETE \
      -H "x-api-key: $GRADIUM_API_KEY" \
      "https://api.gradium.ai/api/voice-generator/embeddings/$CAND1"
    ```

    Safe at any time: a converted voice holds its own copy. An id that is already
    gone returns `404`.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Complete example

The whole flow in one file. Set `GRADIUM_API_KEY` and run it. It creates a
real voice in your account.

<CodeGroup>
  ```python voice_design.py theme={null}
  import os
  import time

  import requests

  BASE_URL = "https://api.gradium.ai/api"
  HEADERS = {"x-api-key": os.environ["GRADIUM_API_KEY"]}

  DESCRIPTION = (
      "A British female voice, 20 to 30, glossy and confident, with high pitch, "
      "fast pacing, high energy and bright sparkling resonance. Ideal for a "
      "friendly receptionist or assistant."
  )
  AUDITION_LINE = "Hi there, thanks so much for calling Northgate! How can I help you today?"


  def check(resp):
      if not resp.ok:
          raise RuntimeError(f"HTTP {resp.status_code}: {resp.text}")
      return resp


  def generate(prompt, language="en", n_samples=3, json_config=None):
      body = {"prompt": prompt, "language": language, "n_samples": n_samples}
      if json_config:
          body["json_config"] = json_config
      resp = check(requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/voice-generator/generate", headers=HEADERS, json=body))
      return [c["embedding_id"] for c in resp.json()["embeddings"]]


  def wait_until_ready(candidate_ids, timeout_s=120.0):
      deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout_s
      pending = set(candidate_ids)
      while pending:
          for candidate_id in sorted(pending):
              resp = check(requests.get(
                  f"{BASE_URL}/voice-generator/embeddings",
                  headers=HEADERS,
                  params={"embedding_id": candidate_id},
              ))
              embeddings = resp.json()["embeddings"]
              if not embeddings:
                  raise RuntimeError(f"candidate {candidate_id} not found")
              if embeddings[0]["ready"]:
  ```
