## Writing a description

The description is the only input the model has. It responds to the attributes a
casting brief would carry, and naming more of them gives a tighter result.

| Attribute | Examples |
| - | - |
| Gender | female, male, androgynous |
| Age | 20 to 30, middle aged, elderly |
| Accent or origin | British, Southern US, Parisian, Brazilian |
| Pitch | high pitch, deep, mid range |
| Pace | fast pacing, measured, unhurried |
| Energy | high energy, calm, subdued |
| Timbre and resonance | glossy, gravelly, breathy, bright sparkling resonance, warm |
| Register and manner | confident, girly chatter, formal, conspiratorial |
| Intended use | a friendly receptionist, an audiobook narrator, a news anchor |

End with the intended use. It steers delivery and register, not only the colour
of the voice.

> A British female voice, 20 to 30, glossy and confident, with girly
> chatter, high pitch, fast pacing, high energy and bright sparkling
> resonance. Ideal for a friendly receptionist or assistant.

### Rules of thumb

* **Use the space.** Up to 500 characters, all usable. Full sentences beat a list of adjectives.
* **Describe the voice, not the script.** Words to be spoken go in the audition line.
* **Set `language` to the language the voice will speak.** It shapes the accent and the delivery, not only the words. Regional accents still go in the description: "Bristolian" or "Parisian" has to be written out.
* **Concrete beats evaluative.** "Low pitch, slow pacing, gravelly" gives the model more than "a great narrator voice".

### Examples

| Voice | Language | Made for |
| :- | :- | :- |
| **Pirate** | English, Bristol | Character narration |
| **Fionn** | English, Ireland | Customer service |
| **Freya** | English, GB | Receptionist |
| **Desmond** | English, US | Long-form narration |

The descriptions as sent:

**Pirate**

> A gruff Bristolian English male pirate voice, 45 to 60, for game and character
> narration: weathered low pitch, gravelly timbre with heavy vocal fry, strong
> projection, at a steady, unhurried pace, boisterous and commanding energy.

**Fionn**

> An Irish English male voice, 40 to 55, for customer service: calm and crisp,
> with mid-low pitch, steady natural pacing, medium energy and warm rounded
> resonance. Ideal for reassuring walkthroughs, empathic de-escalation and
> complex IT support.

**Freya**

> A British female voice, 20 to 30, glossy and confident, with girly chatter,
> high pitch, fast pacing, high energy and bright sparkling resonance. Ideal for
> a friendly receptionist or assistant.

**Desmond**

> An American English male voice, 55 to 65: clean, deliberate and precise, with
> low pitch, slow pacing and low-to-mid energy, resonant timbre and a gentle
> low-to-high flow. Ideal for projecting academic authority.

### Iterating

Edit the attribute that is off rather than rewriting the description.

| Candidates sound... | Change |
| - | - |
| Too young or old | An explicit range: "40 to 55" rather than "middle aged" |
| Too fast or slow | "unhurried", "measured" or "fast pacing" |
| Flat | An energy word and a manner word |
| Too polished | A timbre word: "gravelly", "breathy", "weathered" |
| Right voice, wrong delivery | An intended-use clause at the end |
| Inconsistent with each other | A higher [`cfg_scale`](#cfg_scale) |

### Building this into a product

If you expose voice design to your own users, prefill a form over the
attributes above and compose the sentence from it, with a free-text box as the
escape hatch. Show the 500 character limit. Offer "keep this one" as the way to
hold onto a voice, and make regenerate send a new description rather than more
samples.

## Generation settings

Generation settings shape the voice and go in `json_config` on
`POST /voice-generator/generate`. [Synthesis settings](#synthesis-settings)
shape each utterance and go in `json_config` on the TTS request. Voice Design
still supports `cfg_scale` to control how literally the voice follows your
description.

All generation settings are optional. The defaults are tuned, so send only the
keys you have a reason to change.

```json theme={null}
{
  "prompt": "A calm Irish male voice, 40 to 55, warm and steady, for customer support.",
  "language": "en",
  "n_samples": 3,
  "json_config": { "cfg_scale": 8.0 }
}
```

| Key | Range | Default | Effect |
| - | - | - | - |
| `cfg_scale` | `1.0` to `20.0` | `5.0` | How closely the voice follows the description. Higher is more literal, less varied. |

### `cfg_scale`

* **`5.0`**, the default, when exploring with 3 to 5 candidates and you want them to differ.
* **`8.0` to `12.0`** when candidates drift from the description, or when generating one candidate at a time. Conversational designers that generate one candidate per turn typically use `10.0`.
* **Above `12.0`** the voice follows the description ever more literally at the cost of naturalness, and candidates converge on each other.

`cfg_scale` cannot add an attribute the description does not name. Fix the
[description](#writing-a-description) first.

### The `json_config` allow-list

<Warning>
  Send only `cfg_scale`. **An unknown key or out-of-range value is not rejected.** The request returns `201` and the candidates never become `ready`. Bound your polling loop and treat a timeout as a bad request.

  The usual causes: a synthesis setting such as `temp`, or `cfg_scale` outside its range.
</Warning>

  ```javascript voice_design.mjs theme={null}
        body: JSON.stringify({ text, voice_id: voiceId, output_format: "wav", only_audio: true }),
      }),
    );
    await writeFile(path, Buffer.from(await resp.arrayBuffer()));
  }

  async function convert(candidateId, name, description) {
    const resp = await check(
      await fetch(`${BASE_URL}/voices/from-embedding`, {
        method: "POST",
        headers: HEADERS,
        body: JSON.stringify({ voxium_embedding_id: candidateId, name, description }),
      }),
    );
    return (await resp.json()).uid;
  }

  async function deleteCandidate(candidateId) {
    await fetch(`${BASE_URL}/voice-generator/embeddings/${candidateId}`, {
      method: "DELETE",
      headers: HEADERS,
    });
  }

  console.log("[1/5] generating candidates");
  const candidateIds = await generate(DESCRIPTION, { language: "en", nSamples: 3 });

  console.log("[2/5] waiting until ready");
  await waitUntilReady(candidateIds);

  console.log("[3/5] auditioning");
  for (const [i, candidateId] of candidateIds.entries()) {
    await synthesise(candidateId, AUDITION_LINE, `candidate-${i}.wav`);
    console.log(`      candidate-${i}.wav  ${candidateId}`);
  }

  // Listen to the files, then pick one. This example keeps the first.
  const chosen = candidateIds[0];

  console.log("[4/5] converting the chosen candidate into a voice");
  const voiceId = await convert(chosen, "Receptionist EN", "Front desk and appointment booking");
  console.log(`      voice_id=${voiceId}`);

  console.log("[5/5] synthesising with the new voice");
  await synthesise(
    voiceId,
    "Good morning, and welcome to Northgate! Do you have an appointment with us " +
      "today, or shall I get you booked in?",
    "welcome.wav",
  );

  for (const candidateId of candidateIds) {
    if (candidateId !== chosen) await deleteCandidate(candidateId);
  }
  console.log("done");
  ```
</CodeGroup>

<Note>
  Audio is streamed, so WAV headers carry placeholder lengths. Readers that trust the header, such as Python's `wave`, report a wrong duration. Rewrite the RIFF and `data` sizes after saving if that matters to you.
</Note>

## Writing a description

The description is the only input the model has. It responds to the attributes a
casting brief would carry, and naming more of them gives a tighter result.

| Attribute | Examples |
| - | - |
| Gender | female, male, androgynous |
| Age | 20 to 30, middle aged, elderly |
| Accent or origin | British, Southern US, Parisian, Brazilian |
| Pitch | high pitch, deep, mid range |
| Pace | fast pacing, measured, unhurried |
| Energy | high energy, calm, subdued |
| Timbre and resonance | glossy, gravelly, breathy, bright sparkling resonance, warm |
| Register and manner | confident, girly chatter, formal, conspiratorial |
| Intended use | a friendly receptionist, an audiobook narrator, a news anchor |

End with the intended use. It steers delivery and register, not only the colour
of the voice.

> A British female voice, 20 to 30, glossy and confident, with girly
> chatter, high pitch, fast pacing, high energy and bright sparkling
> resonance. Ideal for a friendly receptionist or assistant.

### Rules of thumb

* **Use the space.** Up to 500 characters, all usable. Full sentences beat a list of adjectives.
* **Describe the voice, not the script.** Words to be spoken go in the audition line.
* **Set `language` to the language the voice will speak.** It shapes the accent and the delivery, not only the words. Regional accents still go in the description: "Bristolian" or "Parisian" has to be written out.
* **Concrete beats evaluative.** "Low pitch, slow pacing, gravelly" gives the model more than "a great narrator voice".

### Examples

| Voice | Language | Made for |
| :- | :- | :- |
| **Pirate** | English, Bristol | Character narration |
| **Fionn** | English, Ireland | Customer service |
| **Freya** | English, GB | Receptionist |
| **Desmond** | English, US | Long-form narration |

The descriptions as sent:

**Pirate**

> A gruff Bristolian English male pirate voice, 45 to 60, for game and character
> narration: weathered low pitch, gravelly timbre with heavy vocal fry, strong
> projection, at a steady, unhurried pace, boisterous and commanding energy.

**Fionn**

> An Irish English male voice, 40 to 55, for customer service: calm and crisp,
> with mid-low pitch, steady natural pacing, medium energy and warm rounded
> resonance. Ideal for reassuring walkthroughs, empathic de-escalation and
> complex IT support.

**Freya**

> A British female voice, 20 to 30, glossy and confident, with girly chatter,
> high pitch, fast pacing, high energy and bright sparkling resonance. Ideal for
> a friendly receptionist or assistant.

**Desmond**

> An American English male voice, 55 to 65: clean, deliberate and precise, with
> low pitch, slow pacing and low-to-mid energy, resonant timbre and a gentle
> low-to-high flow. Ideal for projecting academic authority.

### Iterating

Edit the attribute that is off rather than rewriting the description.

| Candidates sound... | Change |
| - | - |
| Too young or old | An explicit range: "40 to 55" rather than "middle aged" |
| Too fast or slow | "unhurried", "measured" or "fast pacing" |
| Flat | An energy word and a manner word |
| Too polished | A timbre word: "gravelly", "breathy", "weathered" |
| Right voice, wrong delivery | An intended-use clause at the end |
| Inconsistent with each other | A higher [`cfg_scale`](#cfg_scale) |

### Building this into a product

If you expose voice design to your own users, prefill a form over the
attributes above and compose the sentence from it, with a free-text box as the
escape hatch. Show the 500 character limit. Offer "keep this one" as the way to
hold onto a voice, and make regenerate send a new description rather than more
samples.

## Generation settings

Generation settings shape the voice and go in `json_config` on
`POST /voice-generator/generate`. [Synthesis settings](#synthesis-settings)
shape each utterance and go in `json_config` on the TTS request. Voice Design
still supports `cfg_scale` to control how literally the voice follows your
description.

All generation settings are optional. The defaults are tuned, so send only the
keys you have a reason to change.

```json theme={null}
{
  "prompt": "A calm Irish male voice, 40 to 55, warm and steady, for customer support.",
  "language": "en",
  "n_samples": 3,
  "json_config": { "cfg_scale": 8.0 }
}
```

| Key | Range | Default | Effect |
| - | - | - | - |
| `cfg_scale` | `1.0` to `20.0` | `5.0` | How closely the voice follows the description. Higher is more literal, less varied. |

### `cfg_scale`

* **`5.0`**, the default, when exploring with 3 to 5 candidates and you want them to differ.
* **`8.0` to `12.0`** when candidates drift from the description, or when generating one candidate at a time. Conversational designers that generate one candidate per turn typically use `10.0`.
* **Above `12.0`** the voice follows the description ever more literally at the cost of naturalness, and candidates converge on each other.

`cfg_scale` cannot add an attribute the description does not name. Fix the
[description](#writing-a-description) first.

### The `json_config` allow-list

<Warning>
  Send only `cfg_scale`. **An unknown key or out-of-range value is not rejected.** The request returns `201` and the candidates never become `ready`. Bound your polling loop and treat a timeout as a bad request.

  The usual causes: a synthesis setting such as `temp`, or `cfg_scale` outside its range.
</Warning>

def calls(*named: tuple[str, dict]) -> types.GenerateContentResponse:
    parts = [
        types.Part(function_call=types.FunctionCall(id=f"call-{i}", name=name, args=args))

    seen = []

    async def on_status(label):
        seen.append(label)

    return seen, on_status


def function_responses(content: types.Content) -> list[types.FunctionResponse]:
    return [p.function_response for p in content.parts]


async def test_sbb_then_respond(agent, fake, sbb_requests, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.delenv("GEMINI_MODEL", raising=False)
    first = calls(("sbb_connections", SBB_ARGS))
    models = fake(first, calls(("respond", DEMO)))
    seen, on_status = statuses()

    assert await agent.turn("Can I make it?", SCREEN, on_status) == DEMO
    assert seen == ["Checking trains…", "Checking trains…"]  # the prefetch, then the model's own call

    params = sbb_requests[0].url.params
    assert (params["from"], params["to"], params["date"], params["time"], params["limit"]) == (
        "Zürich HB", "Bern", "2026-10-15", "17:55", "4",
    )  # fmt: skip

    user, model, tool = models.calls[1]["contents"]
    assert "<screen_context>" in user.parts[0].text and "Dinner in Bern" in user.parts[0].text
    assert "<trains>" in user.parts[1].text and '"IC 8"' in user.parts[1].text  # prefetched for the plan
    assert user.parts[2].text == "Can I make it?"
    assert model is first.candidates[0].content  # appended unmodified
    (response,) = function_responses(tool)
    assert (response.id, response.name) == ("call-0", "sbb_connections")
    assert response.response["connections"][0] == {
        "line": "IC 8", "from": "Zürich HB", "to": "Bern",
        "departure": "2026-10-15T18:01:00+02:00", "arrival": "2026-10-15T18:58:00+02:00",
        "platform": "31", "arrival_platform": "6", "transfers": 0, "delay_min": 0, "duration_min": 57,
    }  # fmt: skip
    assert len(response.response["connections"]) == 4

    config = models.calls[0]["config"]
    assert models.calls[0]["model"] == "gemini-3.8-flash"
    assert config.temperature is None
    assert config.thinking_config.thinking_level == types.ThinkingLevel.LOW
    assert config.tool_config.function_calling_config.mode == types.FunctionCallingConfigMode.ANY
    assert config.tool_config.function_calling_config.allowed_function_names is None
    assert len(agent.history) == 1 and len(agent.history[0]) == 5  # user, model, tool, model, respond's response


async def test_invalid_cards_retry_once_then_no_cards(agent, fake, sbb_requests):
    bad = {"say": "Take the 18:01.", "cards": [{**DEMO["cards"][1], "departure": "18:01"}]}
    models = fake(calls(("sbb_connections", SBB_ARGS)), calls(("respond", bad)), calls(("respond", bad)))
    seen, on_status = statuses()

    assert await agent.turn("Can I make it?", None, on_status) == {"say": "Take the 18:01.", "cards": []}

    assert len(models.calls) == 3
    (error,) = function_responses(models.calls[2]["contents"][-1])
    assert error.name == "respond" and "departure must be ISO 8601" in error.response["error"]
    last = models.calls[2]["config"].tool_config.function_calling_config
    assert last.mode == types.FunctionCallingConfigMode.ANY and last.allowed_function_names == ["respond"]


async def test_cancelled_turn_leaves_history_unchanged(agent, fake, sbb_requests):
    models = fake(calls(("respond", DEMO)), calls(("sbb_connections", SBB_ARGS)), HANG)
    seen, on_status = statuses()
    await agent.turn("Can I make it?", SCREEN, on_status)
    before = agent.history

    async def second_step_running():
        while len(models.calls) < 3:
            await asyncio.sleep(0)

    task = asyncio.create_task(agent.turn("And the next train?", None, on_status))
    await asyncio.wait_for(second_step_running(), 1)  # the turn has SBB results, not yet respond
    task.cancel()
    with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError):
        await task
    assert agent.history is before and len(before) == 1

(PCM s16le, mono, 24 kHz, base64).

Checks, from backend/:
    uv run python voice.py tts "Hello from the beaver"   # writes out.wav, prints time to first audio
    uv run python voice.py stt out.wav                    # prints the transcript
"""

import asyncio
import base64
import json
import logging
import os
import sys
import time
import wave
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Awaitable, Callable

import certifi

# python.org builds on macOS ship without CA certs. aiohttp (inside gradium) builds its
# TLS context at import time, so this must run before `import gradium`.
os.environ.setdefault("SSL_CERT_FILE", certifi.where())

import aiohttp  # noqa: E402  (gradium's own transport)
import gradium  # noqa: E402

SAMPLE_RATE = 24000
CHUNK_BYTES = 3840  # 80 ms
DEFAULT_VOICE_ID = "JuMRs5W5S52hzuge"  # Cormac: bright, warm, cheerful (flagship catalog)

# Hands-free end of turn, from the semantic VAD in Gradium's `step` messages (one per 80 ms).
END_HORIZON_S = 2.0  # read the `vad` entry with this horizon_s
END_PROB = 0.5  # its inactivity_prob must be above this...
END_STEPS = 3  # ...for this many steps in a row, once the turn has text
REOPEN_AFTER_S = 1.0  # a closed hands-free session reopens on the next audio, at most once a second
BACKLOG_CHUNKS = 25  # hands-free audio waiting for a session: the newest 2 s, older chunks drop

# Gradium keyword boosting for the demo's place names. Case-sensitive, hence the variants.
# Synthetic test voices still say "Bern" like "burn", so the agent also resolves names.
_PLACES = ["Bern", "Zürich", "Zurich", "Basel", "Luzern", "Geneva", "Lausanne"]
KEYWORDS = {"words": _PLACES + [p.lower() for p in _PLACES] + ["SBB"], "boost": 3}

log = logging.getLogger("voice")
_client: gradium.client.GradiumClient | None = None


def client() -> gradium.client.GradiumClient:
    global _client
    if _client is None:
        _client = gradium.client.GradiumClient()  # reads GRADIUM_API_KEY
    return _client


async def speak(text: str) -> AsyncIterator[str]:
    """Yield base64 PCM chunks for `text`. One TTS socket per reply."""
    voice_id = os.environ.get("GRADIUM_VOICE_ID") or DEFAULT_VOICE_ID
    async with client().tts_realtime(
        model_name="default", voice_id=voice_id, output_format="pcm_24000"
    ) as tts:
        await tts.send_text(text)
        await tts.send_eos()
        async for msg in _messages(tts):  # raw frames: base64 audio passes through as is
            if msg["type"] == "audio":
                yield msg["audio"]
            elif msg["type"] == "end_of_stream":
                break


class Transcriber:
    """One push-to-talk turn: push() base64 chunks as they arrive, then finish()."""

    def __init__(self, language: str = "en"):
        self._queue: asyncio.Queue[bytes | None] = asyncio.Queue()
        self._task = asyncio.create_task(self._run(language))

    def push(self, b64: str) -> None:
        self._queue.put_nowait(base64.b64decode(b64))

    async def finish(self) -> str:
        """End of speech: Gradium drains the remaining text, then closes."""
        self._queue.put_nowait(None)
        return await self._task

    def cancel(self) -> None:
        self._task.cancel()

    async def _run(self, language: str) -> str:
        parts: list[str] = []
        async with client().stt_realtime(
            model_name="default", input_format="pcm", json_config={"language": language, "keywords": KEYWORDS}
        ) as stt:

            async def send() -> None:
                while (chunk := await self._queue.get()) is not None:
                    await stt.send_audio(chunk)
                await stt.send_eos()

            sender = asyncio.create_task(send())
            try:
                async for msg in _messages(stt):
                    if msg["type"] == "text":
                        parts.append(msg["text"])
                    elif msg["type"] == "end_of_stream":
                        break
            finally:
                sender.cancel()
        return " ".join(p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip())


async def _messages(stream) -> AsyncIterator[dict]:
    """STT or TTS messages. Use instead of `async for msg in stream`: in gradium 0.6.4 that
    spins forever, freezing the event loop, when the connection drops without a close frame."""
    async for frame in stream._ws:  # aiohttp stops iterating on any close
        if frame.type == aiohttp.WSMsgType.TEXT:
            msg = json.loads(frame.data)
            if msg["type"] == "error":
                raise RuntimeError(f"Gradium error: {msg}")
            yield msg


class TurnDetector:
    """Hands-free end of turn: inactivity_prob at END_HORIZON_S above END_PROB for
    END_STEPS `step`s in a row, counted only once the turn has text."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.words: list[str] = []
        self._streak = 0

    def feed(self, msg: dict) -> bool:
        """One STT message in; True when the turn has ended."""
        if msg["type"] == "text" and msg["text"].strip():
            self.words.append(msg["text"].strip())
        elif msg["type"] == "step" and self.words:
            p = next((v["inactivity_prob"] for v in msg["vad"] if v["horizon_s"] == END_HORIZON_S), 0.0)
            self._streak = self._streak + 1 if p > END_PROB else 0
            return self._streak >= END_STEPS
        return False

    def take(self) -> str:
        """The turn's text; starts the next turn."""
        text, self.words, self._streak = " ".join(self.words), [], 0
        return text


class ContinuousTranscriber:
    """Hands-free: one STT session per WebSocket, open across turns. push() base64 chunks
    for as long as the mic is on. Awaits on_speech() at a turn's first words and
    on_turn(text) at its end. If Gradium closes the session, the next push() reopens it."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        on_speech: Callable[[], Awaitable[None]],
        on_turn: Callable[[str], Awaitable[None]],
        language: str = "en",
    ):
        self._on_speech, self._on_turn, self._language = on_speech, on_turn, language
        self._queue: asyncio.Queue[bytes] = asyncio.Queue(BACKLOG_CHUNKS)
        self._turn = TurnDetector()  # outlives a session, so a turn survives a reopen
        self._task: asyncio.Task | None = None
        self._opened = float("-inf")

    def push(self, b64: str) -> None:
        closed = self._task is None or self._task.done()
        if closed and time.monotonic() - self._opened > REOPEN_AFTER_S:
            self._opened = time.monotonic()
            self._task = asyncio.create_task(self._run())
        if self._queue.full():  # no session drains it: drop the oldest, never replay a stale backlog
            self._queue.get_nowait()
        self._queue.put_nowait(base64.b64decode(b64))

    def cancel(self) -> None:
        if self._task is not None:
            self._task.cancel()

    async def _run(self) -> None:
        try:
            async with client().stt_realtime(
                model_name="default", input_format="pcm", json_config={"language": self._language, "keywords": KEYWORDS}
            ) as stt:

                async def send() -> None:
                    while True:
                        await stt.send_audio(await self._queue.get())

                sender = asyncio.create_task(send())
                try:
                    await self._listen(stt)
                finally:
                    sender.cancel()
        except Exception:
            log.exception("hands-free STT failed")
        log.info("hands-free STT session closed; the next audio reopens it")

    async def _listen(self, stt) -> None:
        # A flush sent on a closed session gets no `flushed`; an ended turn flushes again on the next `step`.
        turn, flushing = self._turn, False
        async for msg in _messages(stt):
            fresh = not turn.words
            ended = turn.feed(msg)
            if fresh and turn.words:
                await self._on_speech()
            if ended and not flushing:  # flush makes Gradium emit the words it holds back
                flushing = True
                await stt.send_flush()
            elif msg["type"] == "flushed" and flushing:
                flushing = False
                await self._on_turn(turn.take())


async def _cli_tts(text: str) -> None:
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    first = None
    pcm = bytearray()
    async for chunk in speak(text):
        first = first or time.monotonic() - t0
        pcm += base64.b64decode(chunk)
    with wave.open("out.wav", "wb") as f:
        f.setnchannels(1)
        f.setsampwidth(2)
        f.setframerate(SAMPLE_RATE)
        f.writeframes(bytes(pcm))
    print(f"out.wav: {len(pcm) / 2 / SAMPLE_RATE:.2f} s audio, first audio after {first:.2f} s")


async def _cli_stt(path: str) -> None:
    with wave.open(path, "rb") as f:
        assert (f.getframerate(), f.getnchannels(), f.getsampwidth()) == (SAMPLE_RATE, 1, 2), "need 24 kHz mono s16"
        pcm = f.readframes(f.getnframes())
    stt = Transcriber()
    for i in range(0, len(pcm), CHUNK_BYTES):  # paced like a live mic
        stt.push(base64.b64encode(pcm[i : i + CHUNK_BYTES]).decode())
        await asyncio.sleep(0.08)
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    text = await stt.finish()
    print(f"transcript ({time.monotonic() - t0:.2f} s after end of audio): {text!r}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from dotenv import load_dotenv

    load_dotenv()
    load_dotenv("../.env")
    cmd, arg = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    asyncio.run(_cli_tts(arg) if cmd == "tts" else _cli_stt(arg))

def test_interrupt_closes_the_tts_stream(client, monkeypatch):
    closed = []

    async def endless_speak(text):
        try:
            for _ in range(10_000):  # never waits, so the interrupt lands at send()
                yield "AAAA"
        finally:
            await asyncio.sleep(0.1)  # the TTS socket's closing handshake
            closed.append(True)

    monkeypatch.setattr(server.voice, "speak", endless_speak)
    ctx, ws = connect(client)

        pass
    ws.send_json({"type": "interrupt"})

import asyncio

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from starlette.websockets import WebSocketDisconnect

import app as server


class FakeTranscriber:
    def __init__(self):
        self.chunks = []

    def push(self, b64):
        self.chunks.append(b64)

    async def finish(self):
        return "Can I make it?" if self.chunks else ""

    def cancel(self):
        pass


class OfflineTranscriber(server.voice.Transcriber):
    """The real push(), which base64-decodes, without opening Gradium."""

    def __init__(self):
        self._queue = asyncio.Queue()

    def cancel(self):
        pass


async def fake_speak(text, voice_id=None):
    for chunk in ("AAAA", "BBBB"):
        yield chunk


async def slow_speak(text, voice_id=None):
    yield "AAAA"
    await asyncio.sleep(5)  # long enough to interrupt
    yield "BBBB"


@pytest.fixture
def client(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("APP_TOKEN", "test-token")
    monkeypatch.setenv("MOCK_AGENT", "1")
    monkeypatch.setattr(server.voice, "speak", fake_speak)
    monkeypatch.setattr(server.voice, "Transcriber", FakeTranscriber)
    return TestClient(server.app)


def connect(client):
    ws = client.websocket_connect("/ws")
    conn = ws.__enter__()
    conn.send_json({"type": "hello", "token": "test-token"})
    assert conn.receive_json() == {"type": "ready"}
    return ws, conn


def receive_turn(ws):
    """Messages up to and including the final `state: idle`."""
    msgs = []
    while True:
        msgs.append(ws.receive_json())
        if msgs[-1] == {"type": "state", "state": "idle"}:
            return msgs


def kinds(msgs):
    return [m["type"] + (":" + m["state"] if m["type"] == "state" else "") for m in msgs]


def test_text_turn_order(client):
    ctx, ws = connect(client)
    ws.send_json({"type": "text", "text": "Can I make it?"})
    msgs = receive_turn(ws)
    ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)
    assert kinds(msgs) == [
        "state:thinking", "state:searching", "reply", "state:speaking",
        "audio", "audio", "audio_end", "state:idle",
    ]
    reply = msgs[2]
    assert [c["kind"] for c in reply["cards"]] == ["conflict", "train"]
    assert msgs[4]["data"] == "AAAA"


def test_voice_turn(client):
    ctx, ws = connect(client)
    ws.send_json({"type": "audio", "data": "AAAA"})
    ws.send_json({"type": "audio", "data": "BBBB"})
    ws.send_json({"type": "audio_end"})
    msgs = receive_turn(ws)
    ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)
    assert kinds(msgs)[:4] == ["state:listening", "transcript", "state:thinking", "state:searching"]
    assert msgs[1]["text"] == "Can I make it?"


def test_audio_end_without_audio_is_ignored(client):
    ctx, ws = connect(client)
    ws.send_json({"type": "audio_end"})  # no audio: ignored
    ws.send_json({"type": "text", "text": "hi"})
    assert ws.receive_json() == {"type": "state", "state": "thinking"}
    ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)


def test_wrong_token_is_rejected(client):
    with client.websocket_connect("/ws") as ws:
        ws.send_json({"type": "hello", "token": "nope"})
        with pytest.raises(WebSocketDisconnect) as exc:
            ws.receive_json()
    assert exc.value.code == 1008


def test_non_dict_hello_is_rejected(client):
    with client.websocket_connect("/ws") as ws:
        ws.send_json(["hello", "test-token"])
        with pytest.raises(WebSocketDisconnect) as exc:
            ws.receive_json()
    assert exc.value.code == 1008


def test_malformed_frames_are_ignored(client):
    ctx, ws = connect(client)
    ws.send_text("{not json")
    ws.send_bytes(b"\x00")
    ws.send_json({"type": "text", "text": "hi"})
    assert ws.receive_json() == {"type": "state", "state": "thinking"}
    ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)


def test_bad_base64_audio_is_ignored(client, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(server.voice, "Transcriber", OfflineTranscriber)
    ctx, ws = connect(client)
    ws.send_json({"type": "audio", "data": "AAA"})  # bad padding: push() raises binascii.Error
    assert ws.receive_json() == {"type": "state", "state": "listening"}
    ws.send_json({"type": "text", "text": "hi"})
    assert ws.receive_json() == {"type": "state", "state": "thinking"}
    ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)


def speak_slowly_until_first_audio(client, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(server.voice, "speak", slow_speak)
    ctx, ws = connect(client)
    ws.send_json({"type": "text", "text": "Can I make it?"})
    while ws.receive_json()["type"] != "audio":
        pass
    return ctx, ws


def test_interrupt_stops_speech(client, monkeypatch):
    ctx, ws = speak_slowly_until_first_audio(client, monkeypatch)
    ws.send_json({"type": "interrupt"})
    assert ws.receive_json() == {"type": "state", "state": "idle"}  # no more audio, no audio_end
    ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)


def test_talking_over_the_mascot_interrupts(client, monkeypatch):
    ctx, ws = speak_slowly_until_first_audio(client, monkeypatch)
    ws.send_json({"type": "audio", "data": "AAAA"})
    assert ws.receive_json() == {"type": "state", "state": "listening"}
    ws.send_json({"type": "audio_end"})
    msgs = receive_turn(ws)
    ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)
    assert kinds(msgs)[:2] == ["transcript", "state:thinking"]


def test_release_replaces_a_text_turn_sent_while_held(client, monkeypatch):
    async def echo(self, text, screen, on_status):
        await asyncio.sleep(1)  # both turns would be in here together
        return {"say": text, "cards": []}

    monkeypatch.setattr(server.StubAgent, "turn", echo)
    ctx, ws = connect(client)
    ws.send_json({"type": "audio", "data": "AAAA"})  # press
    ws.send_json({"type": "text", "text": "Typed while held"})
    ws.send_json({"type": "audio_end"})  # release: the voice turn replaces the text turn
    msgs = receive_turn(ws)
    ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)
    assert [m["say"] for m in msgs if m["type"] == "reply"] == ["Can I make it?"]


def test_interrupt_closes_the_tts_stream(client, monkeypatch):
    closed = []

    async def endless_speak(text, voice_id=None):
        try:
            for _ in range(10_000):  # never waits, so the interrupt lands at send()
                yield "AAAA"
        finally:
            await asyncio.sleep(0.1)  # the TTS socket's closing handshake
            closed.append(True)

    monkeypatch.setattr(server.voice, "speak", endless_speak)
    ctx, ws = connect(client)
    ws.send_json({"type": "text", "text": "Can I make it?"})
    while ws.receive_json()["type"] != "audio":
        pass
    ws.send_json({"type": "interrupt"})
    msgs = receive_turn(ws)
    assert closed == [True]  # before the idle, not later through GC
    ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)
    assert "audio_end" not in kinds(msgs)

def calls(*named: tuple[str, dict]) -> types.GenerateContentResponse:
    parts = [
        types.Part(function_call=types.FunctionCall(id=f"call-{i}", name=name, args=args))
        for i, (name, args) in enumerate(named)
    ]
    return types.GenerateContentResponse(candidates=[types.Candidate(content=types.Content(role="model", parts=parts))])


class FakeModels:
    def __init__(self, *steps):
        self.steps = list(steps)
        self.calls = []

    async def generate_content(self, **kwargs):
        self.calls.append({**kwargs, "contents": list(kwargs["contents"])})
        step = self.steps.pop(0)
        if step is HANG:
            await asyncio.Event().wait()
        if isinstance(step, Exception):
            raise step
        return step

content.text:
The voice-design tool works end to end against the live APIs. Asked to "talk like a grumpy old Swiss train conductor", the agent made itself that voice and then answered in it. It's committed as `a501211` on `feature/wp2-voice-design`, in the worktree `.claude/worktrees/voice-design`, branched from `origin/develop`. I haven't pushed it.

**How it works**
- **`design_voice` tool** in [dev_agent.py](backend/dev_agent.py): Gemini writes a description of the voice and the agent keeps the resulting voice for the rest of the session.
- **`voice.design_voice()`** in [voice.py](backend/voice.py): asks Gradium for one candidate voice, waits up to 30 s for it, then converts it into a permanent `voice_id`.
- **Replies carry `voice_id`**: every reply after that includes it, and [app.py](backend/app.py) passes it to `speak()`. I added it to the reply format in [contracts.md](docs/contracts.md) in the same commit.
- **CLI**: `uv run python voice.py design "<brief>"` designs a voice and writes a sample to `out.wav`.

**Tests**
- 110 offline tests pass: the 105 existing ones plus 5 new ones covering the wait-and-convert flow, the timeout, the agent tool, a failed design, and the voice reaching TTS.
- In the live run, the turn took 11.2 s:

  | Step | Time |
  | --- | --- |
  | Gemini decides to call `design_voice` | 4.3 s |
  | Gradium designs and converts the voice | 3.8 s |
  | Gemini writes the reply | 3.0 s |

  Streaming TTS in the new voice started after 0.36 s. I sent you the audio.

**Limits to know**
- **Voice slots fill up.** Each design permanently uses one of your custom-voice slots, and the code never frees them. Gradium returns a 409 error once you hit your limit. The live test used one slot, voice `YlJ3vKdMECZ965Ee`.
- **The voice doesn't persist.** It resets to the default when the WebSocket session ends.
- **Only DevAgent has the tool.** WP3's `agent.py` would need the same tool when it lands.
- **No Italian.** Gradium can only design voices in English, French, Spanish, Portuguese and German.

If repeated demos start hitting the slot limit, the fix is to delete the old voice whenever a new one replaces it.
